analysis.title: Marriott International (MAR): First Take: Strong results with 3Q26 beat and guidance raise ahead of expectations
key_insights: MAR reported 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of $1.512bn, above GSe/consensus of ~$1.48bn/$1.47bn (+12% y/y) and above the high end of its prior guidance range of $1.44bn to $1.47bn. The beat was driven mainly by higher than expected incentive management fees (IMFs) and base management fees.

System-wide constant-$ RevPAR grew +6.5% y/y vs GSe 5.3% and consensus 4.5%, and well above MAR's 3Q guidance range of +3.5% to +4.0%. US & Canada +7.4%, Europe +6.4%, ME&A -5.3%, Greater China -0.3%, APEC ex China +9.3%, CALA +3.2%, International +4.4%.
Adjusted diluted EPS of $3.02 beat GSe/consensus of $2.83/$2.85 and the prior guidance range of $2.74 to $2.82. MAR repurchased $1.3bn of stock in 3Q vs $1.1bn in 2Q26.

Net rooms growth was 4.6% y/y vs GSe/consensus of 4.4%/4.4%. The global pipeline rose +0.8% sequentially to about 634k rooms. The in-construction pipeline fell about 0.4% sequentially to over 278k and grew +11.2% y/y.

MAR raised 2026 system-wide RevPAR growth guidance to +4.5% to +5.0% from +3.0% to +3.5%, vs consensus of 3.6%. GS estimates about half of the raise comes from 3Q outperformance and the rest from a better 4Q outlook.
MAR raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $6,075mn-$6,098mn from $5,965mn-$6,025mn, vs consensus of $6,016mn. GS estimates about 2/3 of the raise comes from 3Q outperformance.

MAR raised 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $12.07-$12.14 from $11.64-$11.81, vs consensus of $11.76. Gross fee revenue guidance rose to $6,137mn-$6,145mn from $6,025mn-$6,055mn, vs consensus of $6,060mn.

The 4Q26 outlook is largely above consensus: RevPAR +4.5% to +5.0% (consensus 2.7%), gross fee revenue $1,604mn-$1,612mn (consensus $1,558mn), adjusted EBITDA $1,573mn-$1,596mn (consensus $1,554mn), adjusted EPS $3.14-$3.21 (consensus $3.03).

GS calls MAR the cleanest print of the lodging earnings season. The roughly 1.5ppt RevPAR guidance raise flowed through to EBITDA as it should, IMF rose +22% y/y with all regions positive, there was no increase in key money guidance, and capital returns rose by about $300mn. GS expects the stock to outperform.

GS rates MAR Buy with a 12-month price target of $406, based on SOTP: 18.5x 2027E EV/EBITDA for management and franchise fees, 8.5x for owned and leased, and 8x for unallocated/corporate expenses, all unchanged. The stock closed at $399.30 on 30 Oct 2026, implying 1.7% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and a $406 target after a 3Q26 beat and guidance raise, and expects the stock to outperform. Implied upside to the target is only 1.7% from $399.30.

sector_views.rationale: GS calls MAR the cleanest lodging print of the earnings season, with RevPAR, fees and unit growth all ahead of expectations.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA reported $1.512bn vs GSe $1.479bn and consensus $1.472bn (Visible Alpha), +12.1% y/y.
3Q26 adjusted diluted EPS reported $3.02 (per management) vs GSe $2.83 and consensus $2.85, +22.3% y/y. The prior guidance range was $2.74 to $2.82.

3Q26 reported incentive management fees $181mn vs GSe $161mn and consensus $163mn, +22.3% y/y. Base management fees were $334mn vs GSe $324mn. Franchise fees were $1,007mn, in line with consensus. Total gross fees were $1,522mn vs GSe $1,500mn.
3Q26 reported net revenue $1,925mn vs GSe and consensus of $1,875mn, +11.3% y/y. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 78.5%.

FY26 guidance (company outlook, updated 11/2): adjusted EBITDA $6,075mn-$6,098mn (prior $5,965mn-$6,025mn, consensus $6,016mn, GSe $6,025mn), adjusted EPS $12.07-$12.14 (prior $11.64-$11.81, consensus $11.76), capital return to shareholders at least $4,800mn (prior over $4,500mn).
4Q26 guidance (company outlook): adjusted EBITDA $1,573mn-$1,596mn vs GSe $1,561mn and consensus $1,554mn, adjusted EPS $3.14-$3.21 vs GSe $2.99 and consensus $3.03.
risk_factors: A weakening consumer could slow travel demand and pressure ADRs and occupancy.
Softer-than-expected RevPAR growth would directly hurt profitability and margins.
Slower-than-expected unit growth would lower the top line and profitability versus GS forecasts.
Higher industry supply could hurt pricing and occupancy disproportionately.
